title: Per-chain integration tests including crash-mid-batch verifying cursor invariant
description:
Write the per-chain integration test suite using testnet/regtest fixtures, with explicit crash-mid-batch tests proving the §14.4 idempotency invariant. P1 — this is the definitive verification that the tracker is crash-safe (§19 v3.1 row 'Tracker crash safety: Explicit cursor invariant').

What to do:
- For each chain watcher (§17.4 #25–#35 as applicable): build a reproducible fixture environment:
  - EVM: local anvil/hardhat or a mocked Alchemy that replays canned responses.
  - BTC: BTCPay Server in regtest mode or a mocked BTCPay HTTP client.
  - Solana: solana-test-validator or mocked Helius.
  - Zcash-t: zcashd regtest or mocked RPC.
  - Zcash-z: mocked zcashd with viewing-key note decryption fixture.
  - XMR: monero stagenet or mocked monero-wallet-rpc.
- Standard tests per chain: N events in the fixture → all N appear in donations / matching_contributions, cursor advances correctly.
- Crash-mid-batch test pattern (§14.4 critical):
  1. Run watcher with M events available.
  2. Inject a failure inside the DB transaction after K of M events are processed (e.g. throw from a wrapped recordDonation on the K+1th call).
  3. Verify: 0 donations committed, cursor unchanged, last_run_status='error'.
  4. Remove the injected failure, run again.
  5. Verify: all M events now in donations (UNIQUE catches any attempted dupes), cursor advanced, no duplicate rows.
- End-to-end integration scenario: the staging-E2E equivalent of 'send $1 to each chain' (§17.11 #89) is out of scope here; this story focuses on deterministic test-harness integration tests.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every chain watcher (launch-required: BTC, EVM native + L2s, Solana native, Zcash-t, XMR) has a crash-mid-batch test that passes.
- Tests run in CI (GitLab CI per §17.1 #2).
- Test runtime stays reasonable (<5 min total in CI) — use mocked RPCs where local testnets are too heavy.
- Documented: how to run the suite locally (docker-compose per §17.1 #4).

Spec refs: §14.4 idempotency invariant (this story validates it), §17.1 #2 CI, §17.1 #4 local dev, §19 v3.1 table row on crash safety.
Blocked by Drizzle schema (§17.2 #10).

title: Implement encrypted-at-rest storage in TPA secret store
description:
Implement the storage layer that the upload endpoint (story 45) and the tracker startup loader (§17.3 story 22) talk to. All view keys live encrypted at rest in TPA's existing secret store per §10.2; the tracker container holds the only credentials to fetch them.

What to do:
- Integrate with whichever TPA secret store is selected (§18.4 open question — coordinate with Anarcat + Tor finance). Concrete impl behind the secrets/store.ts interface (§14.1) so the rest of the code depends on the interface, not the vendor.
- Write path: accept (chain, owner, view_key_value) and return an opaque view_key_secret_ref like vault://kv/tor-campaign/xmr/anti-censorship/view_key (§10.2). Never echo the value back.
- Read path: given an opaque ref, return the key material in a short-lived in-memory buffer. Used only by story 22's startup loader; no caller writes the value to disk or logs.
- NEVER-LOG-VIEW-KEYS rule: enforce at the interface boundary — the type wrapping the secret must not implement toString/JSON serialization that reveals the value. Test with: accidentally log a SecretString should produce '[REDACTED]'.
- Emit audit entries on both write and read paths (see story 47).
- Supports deletion for story 48's 90-day destruction job.

Acceptance:
- secrets/store.ts interface + concrete TPA-secret-store implementation.
- Write returns an opaque ref; ref stored in donation_addresses.view_key_secret_ref.
- Read returns key material only to in-memory consumer; any accidental log attempt redacts.
- Unit tests with a mocked secret store covering write, read, delete paths and the redaction guarantee.
- Integration test against staging secret store instance (or a compatible stub).

Spec refs: §10.2 storage, §10.3 use, §14.1 secrets/store.ts, §15.2 view keys treated as secrets, §17.6 story 46. Depends on story 45 (upload endpoint is the primary caller of the write path).

title: Address npm audit vulnerabilities (drizzle-orm SQL-inject, fastify DoS/spoofing, next DoS)
description:
npm i reports 14 vulns (8 moderate, 6 high). Triage:

Runtime HIGH (must fix):
- drizzle-orm ^0.33.0 → 0.45.2+. GHSA-gpj5-g38j-94v9 — SQL injection via improperly escaped SQL identifiers. We use drizzle in apps/tracker (schema.ts, client.ts, watcher-state.ts, record-donation.ts, record-matching-contribution.ts). Breaking major.
- fastify ^4.28.1 → 5.8.5+. GHSA-mrq3-vjjr-p77c (DoS sendWebStream), GHSA-jx2c-rxcm-jvmq (Content-Type tab bypass), GHSA-444r-cwp2-x5xf (X-Forwarded-Proto/Host spoof). Used by apps/tracker/src/admin/server.ts. Breaking major 4→5.
- next ^14.2.13 → 15.x or 16.x. Multiple DoS GHSAs (image optimizer, RSC, rewrites, image cache, server components). Static-export mitigates runtime paths but build-time still uses next. Two-major jump via audit-fix — prefer 14→15 first.

Dev-only (lower priority):
- esbuild/vite/vitest (transitive via drizzle-kit + vitest) — dev server only
- drizzle-kit 0.24 → 0.31 (migrations tool)
- glob / eslint-config-next — lint only

Do NOT run `npm audit fix --force` — bumps all four majors at once. Upgrade deliberately:
1. drizzle-orm + drizzle-kit together (verify schema.ts compiles, tests pass)
2. fastify 4→5 (check admin/server.ts API changes, esp. plugin registration and schema validation)
3. next 14→15, then 15→16 (check pages router + output:export still supported; eslint-config-next bundled)

Verify after each: `npm run check` + `npm test`.
notes: Completed 2026-04-22. Upgrades applied: - drizzle-orm 0.33.0 → 0.45.2 (fixes GHSA-gpj5-g38j-94v9 SQL-inject identifier escaping) - drizzle-kit 0.24.2 → 0.31.10 (fixes transitive esbuild dev-server) - fastify 4.28.1 → 5.8.5 (fixes GHSA-mrq3-vjjr-p77c DoS, -jx2c-rxcm-jvmq CT-bypass, -444r-cwp2-x5xf host spoof) - next 14.2.13 → 15.5.15 (covers all 5 next DoS GHSAs — advisory range was 9.5.0 - 15.5.14, 15.5.15+ is safe; no need to jump to 16) - eslint-config-next 14 → 15.5.15 Changes: - apps/tracker/package.json: drizzle-orm, drizzle-kit, fastify bumped - apps/web/package.json: next, eslint-config-next bumped - apps/web/.eslintrc.json: added "next/typescript" extend (Next 15 split TS rules out of core-web-vitals) - package.json (root): added drizzle-orm to devDependencies — WORKAROUND for npm workspace hoisting. drizzle-kit 0.31 has a runtime version check via `import("drizzle-orm/version")`. When drizzle-kit hoists to root but drizzle-orm stays in the workspace (default npm behavior), the import fails. Declaring drizzle-orm at root forces it to hoist alongside drizzle-kit. Safe: it's only used by the tracker workspace. Tried install-strategy=nested first but npm still hoists workspace-declared deps. - apps/tracker/src/db/migrations/0001_small_toxin.sql + 0001_snapshot.json: drizzle-kit 0.31 generated a one-time normalize migration that rebuilds donations/matching_contributions/watcher_state with the new-style CHECK constraint expressions. No-op on empty tables (pre-deployment). Kept rather than deleting 0000 (committed). Verification: - npm run typecheck: clean across @tor/tracker, @tor/web, @tor/types - npm --workspace @tor/tracker run test: 7/7 pass - npm --workspace @tor/web run build: 11 static pages exported cleanly (no regression; one pre-existing warning in SponsorStrip.tsx unrelated) - npm --workspace @tor/tracker run build: compiles clean - npm --workspace @tor/tracker run db:generate: works; schema introspects to 8 tables, no unexpected deltas after the 0001 Remaining vulns (not fixed, all dev-only transitive moderate): - esbuild ≤0.24.2 via drizzle-kit's @esbuild-kit + vitest's vite. Dev-server only (GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99: browser → dev server cross-origin). Does not ship to production. Tracking separately if ever noisy. Deprecation noted (not blocking): - `next lint` deprecated; removed in Next 16. When upgrading to Next 16, migrate to ESLint CLI per https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/eslint

title: matching/compute.ts: square-root matching against dynamic pool
description:

What to do:
- Input: current donations (included_in_match=1), current matching_contributions, list of matching-eligible projects.
- For each project P:
  - donors_P: dedupe by source_address on public-chain donations; each privacy-chain donation counts as its own donor (§12.1, §12.4).
  - total_d_P = Σ amount_usd per donor to P.
  - project_score_P = (Σ sqrt(total_d_P))^2.
- total_score = Σ project_score_P.
- match_P = (project_score_P / total_score) * TotalMatchingPoolUSD (§12.2).
- Return { project_id → projected_match_usd }.
- Pure function; reads from Drizzle but does no writes. Called by snapshot writer (§17.3 #19).

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests with fixtures covering: single donor single project, many small donors vs one whale (sqrt effect), privacy-chain treated as unique donors, zero-donation project (match=0), total_score=0 edge case (return 0 per project).
- Matches worked examples from §12.1/§12.2 with ≤ 0.01 USD rounding tolerance.
- Respects included_in_match=0 (sybil-flagged donations excluded).
- Only sums matching_contributions from matching-eligible chains per §11.5.

Spec refs: §11.5, §12.1, §12.2, §12.4 (privacy-chain tradeoff), §12.5 (used for live projected match), §14.1.

title: View Key Operations
description:
Epic covering the View Key Operations track (spec §17.6, stories 44–48). Monero and shielded Zcash require recipients to provide private view keys so the tracker can observe incoming transfers without any spend authority. View keys arrive from recipients through a TPA-controlled secure channel (encrypted email to a designated key, or upload form on TLS+auth admin endpoint — never via the public site or shared chat), are stored encrypted at rest in TPA's existing secret store (with donation_addresses.view_key_secret_ref holding an opaque reference like vault://kv/tor-campaign/xmr/anti-censorship/view_key), loaded into tracker memory at startup and used only with local monero-wallet-rpc / zcashd instances, NEVER logged, NEVER sent off-host, and destroyed from the secret store 90 days after round close (configurable per recipient).

Child work: document the secure submission process, build the TLS+auth admin upload endpoint, implement encrypted-at-rest storage, add audit logging for every view-key access (who/when/which key — never the value), and build the 90-day destruction job.

Spec refs: §6.1 privacy-chain eligibility, §10 full section (collection, storage, use, rotation, risk acknowledgment), §14.3 admin endpoints, §15.2 view keys treated as secrets, §15.4 rate limiting on admin, §15.10 view key destruction, §17.6. Closes when all child tasks (stories 44–48) close.

title: BaseWatcher abstract class enforcing §14.4 cursor invariant
description:
Implement the BaseWatcher abstract class in src/watchers/base.ts. This is the single most load-bearing piece of the tracker and P1 — it encodes the §14.4 idempotency invariant so individual chain watchers can't get it wrong.

What to do:
- Abstract method fetchEvents(cursor) implemented per chain: returns events strictly after cursor, plus the highest block/ts fully covered.
- Abstract method processEvent(tx, event) implemented per chain: inserts donation/matching_contribution rows via recordDonation / recordMatchingContribution (§17.3 #17, #18).
- Concrete run() method that implements the canonical loop:
  1. read watcher_state (§17.3 #15).
  2. fetchEvents(cursor).
  3. BEGIN single DB transaction.
  4. for each event: call processEvent(tx, event). UNIQUE constraints on donations(chain, tx_hash, project_id) and matching_contributions(chain, tx_hash) are our safety net; on conflict, log + skip (don't error — this is the replay-after-crash path).
  5. In the SAME transaction, call watcherState.advance(tx, ...) with the highest fully-processed height/timestamp.
  6. COMMIT.
- Error handling: if fetchEvents throws, markError() and exit (no cursor advance). If processEvent throws a non-UNIQUE error, rollback and markError. Partial batch is safe because of UNIQUE replay.
- Structured logging: batch size, highest height processed, duration.

Acceptance criteria:
- Integration test using a fake chain source that returns N events: crash (throw) after inserting K<N events inside the transaction → cursor unchanged, no partial donations committed.
- Integration test: replay after crash inserts remaining events, advances cursor, no duplicates (UNIQUE catches them).
- Integration test: fetchEvents throwing leaves cursor unchanged and sets last_run_status='error'.

Spec refs: §3.2, §14.1 (watchers/ layout), §14.4 idempotency invariant (the whole point of this task).
Blocked by Drizzle schema (§17.2 #10).

- Types must encode that advance() takes a tx handle so it can't accidentally be called outside a transaction.

Acceptance criteria:
- Integration test: advance() called inside a transaction that throws does NOT persist the new cursor (rollback behavior).

title: Cursor invariant tests: kill the watcher mid-batch, restart, verify no duplicates and no missed events
description:
Stress-test the §14.4 idempotency invariant — the single most important correctness property of the tracker. The watcher loop MUST advance watcher_state.last_processed_height only on events fully committed in the same DB transaction as the donation/contribution inserts. This test proves that property holds under forced crashes.

WHAT TO DO — TEST CONSTRUCTION:
1. Set up a test harness that drives a watcher against a seeded chain state with a known, ordered set of N incoming events (e.g. 50 test donations queued on a local testnet address or a mock chain client that replays a fixed sequence).
2. For each of the following kill points, run a test case that:
   - Starts the watcher fresh (clean watcher_state row).
   - Lets it process a subset of events.
   - Sends SIGKILL (not SIGTERM — no clean shutdown) at the target kill point.
   - Restarts the watcher from the persisted watcher_state.
   - Lets it run to completion.
   - Asserts the final DB state is identical to a reference run with no kills.

KILL POINTS TO EXERCISE:
- A. After chain query, before DB transaction opens.
- B. Inside the DB transaction after partial inserts, before COMMIT (crash should roll back — cursor must NOT have advanced).
- C. Mid-batch: after the transaction commits but before the process loops to the next batch.
- D. During the second batch of a multi-batch run.
- E. Repeated kill/restart in a tight loop (5x) to expose any ordering bugs.

WHAT THE TEST MUST VERIFY (acceptance criteria):
- **No duplicates**: after all restarts, COUNT(*) in donations/matching_contributions equals exactly N. UNIQUE(chain, tx_hash, project_id) and UNIQUE(chain, tx_hash) constraints never fire on final reconciliation run (or if they do during a replay, they fail loudly and are caught, not silently swallowed).
- **No missed events**: every one of the N seeded events ends up as exactly one row in the DB.
- **Cursor never advances past unprocessed events**: at every kill point, watcher_state.last_processed_height ≤ the height of the highest fully-committed event. Never ahead of committed data.
- **Atomicity**: cursor advance is in the same DB transaction as the inserts (kill point B must leave cursor unchanged even if partial inserts were attempted).
- **Reorg safety** (§14.4 last paragraph): for EVM/Solana watchers, confirm cursor tracks (head - confirmation_depth), not latest head.

DEPENDENCIES:
- Depends on story 89 (watcher infra exercised and functional on staging).

CROSS-TRACK (context only):
- Depends on BaseWatcher + watcher_state helpers (§17.3).
- Per-chain watchers from §17.4.

Spec: docs/tech-spec-v3.1.md §14.4, §8.6, §17.11 story 91. This is the 'single most important correctness property' per §14.4.
